chunks: Saʿd, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:

I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a man from the cloth merchants entered upon him and said: “May I be your ransom, profits, wealth, and trade come into our hands, and we know that your right in them is established, yet we have been falling short regarding that.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “We would not be dealing fairly with you if we were to impose that upon you today.”

key_terms.الْأَرْبَاحُ: profits or gains acquired through earning
key_terms.الْأَمْوَالُ: wealths or monetary assets in one's possession
key_terms.الْيَوْمَ: at this present time or current circumstance
key_terms.حَقَّكَ: your established right, referring here to the Imam’s due
key_terms.كَلَّفْنَاكُمْ: we imposed or obligated you with something burdensome
key_terms.مُقَصِّرُونَ: falling short or being negligent in fulfilling an obligation

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permit leniency regarding khums on profits and trade for the Shi'ah?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a man acknowledging the established right of the Imam عليه السلام in profits, wealth, and trade, while admitting deficiency in fulfilling it. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام responds by indicating leniency, saying it would not be fair to burden them with that at that time, which relates to the discussion of khums for the Shi'ah in the state of ghaybah.
